# Commands

The packet layer. Obtain the instance with `VescIf.commands()`; do not construct a new one, it would not be connected to the device. Slots are listed with the invokables because QML calls both the same way.

Values arrive as signals, never as properties: connect `Connections { target: VescIf.commands(); function onValuesReceived(values, mask) {...} }` and start the stream with `mCommands.getValues()` (once per interval, not per frame).

Signatures use C++ types. In QML: `QString` is a JS string, `QVector<T>` and `QStringList` are JS arrays, `QVariantMap` is a plain JS object, `QVariantList` an array, `QByteArray` an `ArrayBuffer` (read with a `DataView`), and `QVariant` anything.

Generated from vesc_tool `a34c1727` (working tree dirty).
